form.current-chamber: IN THE SENATE OF THE UNITED STATES

action.action-desc: Received; read twice and referred to the Committee on Banking, Housing, and Urban Affairs

form.official-title: To direct the Commodity Futures Trading Commission and the Securities and Exchange Commission to jointly establish a digital asset working group, and for other purposes.

section.text: This Act may be cited as the Eliminate Barriers to Innovation Act of 2021 .

section.header: Working Group to support innovation with respect to digital assets

subsection.text: Not later than 90 days after the date of the enactment of this section, the Securities and Exchange Commission and the Commodity Futures Trading Commission shall jointly establish a working group (to be known as the SEC and CFTC Working Group on Digital Assets) to carry out the report required under subsection (c)(1).

paragraph.text: The Working Group shall be composed of members appointed in accordance with paragraph (2).

subparagraph.text: The Securities and Exchange Commission and the Commodity Futures Trading Commission shall each appoint an equal number of employees of each such Commission to serve as members of the Working Group.

clause.text: The Securities and Exchange Commission and the Commodity Futures Trading Commission shall each appoint an equal number of nongovernmental representatives to serve as members of the Working Group, except that such number of members may not be greater than or equal to the number of members appointed under subparagraph (A).
The members of the Working Group appointed under clause (i) shall include at least one representative from each of the following:

subclause.text: Financial technology companies that provide products or services involving digital assets.
Financial firms under the jurisdiction of the Securities and Exchange Commission or the Commodity Futures Trading Commission.
Institutions or organizations engaged in academic research or advocacy relating to digital asset use.
Small businesses engaged in financial technology.
Institutions and organizations that support investment in historically-underserved businesses.

subparagraph.header: No compensation for members of the Working Group

clause.text: All members of the Working Group appointed under subparagraph (A) shall serve without compensation in addition to that received for their services as officers or employees of the United States.
All members of the Working Group appointed under subparagraph (B) shall serve without compensation.

paragraph.text: Not later than 1 year after the date of the enactment of this section, the Working Group shall submit to the Securities and Exchange Commission, the Commodity Futures Trading Commission, and the relevant committees a report that contains—

clause.text: the legal and regulatory framework and related developments in the United States relating to digital assets, including—

subclause.text: the impact that lack of clarity in such framework has on primary and secondary markets in digital assets; and
how the domestic legal and regulatory regimes relating to digital assets impact the competitive position of the United States; and

clause.text: developments in other countries related to digital assets and identification of how these developments impact the competitive position of the United States; and

for the creation, maintenance, and improvement of primary and secondary markets in digital assets, including for improving the fairness, orderliness, integrity, efficiency, transparency, availability, and efficacy of such markets;
for standards concerning custody, private key management, cybersecurity, and business continuity relating to digital asset intermediaries; and

subclause.text: reduce fraud and manipulation of digital assets in cash, leveraged, and derivatives markets;
improve investor protections for participants in such markets; and
assist in compliance with anti-money laundering and countering the financing of terrorism obligations under the Bank Secrecy Act.

paragraph.header: Report limited to SEC and CFTC authorities
paragraph.text: The analysis and recommendations provided under subparagraphs (A) and (B) of paragraph (1) may only relate to the laws, regulations, and related matters that are under the primary jurisdiction of the Securities and Exchange Commission or the Commodity Futures Trading Commission.

subsection.text: The Federal Advisory Committee Act (5 U.S.C. App.) shall not apply to the Working Group.

paragraph.text: The Working Group shall terminate on the date that is 1 year after the date of the enactment of this section, except that the Chairman of the Securities and Exchange Commission and the Chairman of the Commodity Futures Trading Commission may, jointly, extend the Working Group for a longer period, not to exceed 1 year.

paragraph.header: Second report in the case of extension
paragraph.text: In the case of an extension of the Working Group under paragraph (1), the Working Group shall, not later than the last day of such extension, submit to the Securities and Exchange Commission, the Commodity Futures Trading Commission, and the relevant committees a report that contains an update to the analysis and recommendations required under subparagraphs (A) and (B) of subsection (c)(1).
The term Bank Secrecy Act means—

subparagraph.text: section 21 of the Federal Deposit Insurance Act (12 U.S.C. 1829b);
chapter 2 of title I of Public Law 91–508 (12 U.S.C. 1951 et seq.); and
subchapter II of chapter 53 of title 31, United States Code.

paragraph.text: The term historically-underserved businesses means women-owned businesses, minority-owned businesses, and rural businesses.

subparagraph.text: the Committee on Financial Services of the House of Representatives;
the Committee on Banking, Housing, and Urban Affairs of the Senate;
the Committee on Agriculture of the House of Representatives; and
the Committee on Agriculture, Nutrition, and Forestry of the Senate.

paragraph.text: The term Working Group means the working group established under subsection (a).

attestation-group.attestation-date: Passed the House of Representatives April 20, 2021.
